links.outcome: AUROC of pediatric CLABSI model on retrospective versus prospective deployment data
links.effect: AUROC fell from 0.97 on retrospective data to <0.60 in offline deployment validation; feature leakage and overfitting were among primary root causes.
links.quote: The area under the receiver-operating characteristic (AUROC) fell from 0.97 from retrospective data to <0.60 despite multiple iterations of troubleshooting.

links.outcome: Compatibility of model input features between development data and real-time production data
links.effect: Train/serve skew and challenging feature translation between real-time and historical data models caused performance to fall from AUROC 0.97 to <0.60.
links.quote: Primary root causes included train/serve skew, feature leakage, and overfitting.

unlisted_practices: Early coordination between data governance, data science, clinical informatics and implementation engineers during model development
Balancing predictive performance against implementation feasibility (model complexity) during development
Building monitoring and logging infrastructure to troubleshoot deployed models

screen.reason: Evaluates the transition of a predictive risk model from retrospective development to pre-deployment prospective validation, identifying performance degradation (train/serve skew, feature leakage) and analyzing deployment safeguards.

primary.practice: pre-deployment prospective offline validation and root-cause analysis of train-serve skew
